title: Finite-free duality for component-lift coefficients
statement: For every commutative condensed ring Lambda, every scheme T, and every internal Lambda_T-module L which is pro-etale locally finite free [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], ComponentLiftLisseFacts Lambda T L [def-sfb-component-lift-section-data] holds: there is a locally finite free P with an ordinary ExactPairing L P, both degree-zero complexes are K-flat for the actual module tensor, and their singleFunctor images admit an ExactPairing in the ordinary derived category. No affineness or contractibility hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Old proof steps 4-6; HRS Definition 3.3, Lemma 4.1, Proposition 4.3(3) and equation (4.2); Stacks Tag 08JJ, sites-cohomology.tex label lemma-dual-perfect-complex, global Hom formula at the coefficient unit. Agent-formulated map normalization for component lifts.

proof.text: For the given scheme T and lisse module L, construct P as the internal module Hom from L to the regular coefficient module. On a finite-free trivializing slice P is the finite coordinate dual of L and is therefore lisse. The finite-free tensor-exactness theorem applies to L and P, with the commutative internal coefficient ring Lambda_T. Their tensor functors preserve finite limits and cokernels (the latter by the tensor universal property), so both modules are flat. For every acyclic complex A, exactness gives H^n(A tensor L)=H^n(A) tensor L=0, and likewise for P. The single degree-zero complexes of L and P are therefore K-flat. Their terms, finite tensor products and the coefficient unit are flat; K-flat tensor descent computes their derived tensors by the corresponding ordinary single complexes.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, finite-free local calculation; degree-zero K-flatness via exact tensor.

proof.text: On every finite-free slice, evaluation sends phi tensor x to phi(x), and coevaluation sends 1 to sum_i e_i tensor e_i^*. Under a change of coordinates with mutually inverse matrices A,B, the coefficient of e_i tensor e_k^* in this sum becomes sum_j A_ij B_jk=delta_ik; this also handles rectangular inverse matrices. Hence the local coevaluations agree on overlaps and glue, since the Hom presheaf is a sheaf. The two triangle composites are x↦sum_i e_i e_i^*(x)=x and phi↦sum_i phi(e_i)e_i^*=phi. These equalities are local, so they hold globally, giving ExactPairing L P. The K-flat tensor comparison from the first step transports these maps and identities to the ordinary derived category, giving the required ExactPairing of the singleFunctor images. For rank zero the sums are empty; varying ranks are handled on the respective slices.
